\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{دم} \fa{کردن} (dam kardan)}{دم کردن (dam kardan)}]{\fa{دم} \fa{کردن} (dam kardan) — to brew (tea); to steam (rice)}

\label{lesson:FA-C218-dam-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to walk, then the Persian for to get on.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{دم} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{دم} \fa{کردن}} — \emph{dam kardan} — \textquotedblleft{}to brew (tea); to steam (rice)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dam kardan} pairs \emph{dam}, \textquotedblleft{}breath, steam\textquotedblright{}, a native word, with \emph{kardan}: to let it steam. (EtymDB also lists Arabic \emph{dam}, \textquotedblleft{}blood\textquotedblright{}, a different word that looks alike.) \emph{kardan}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}, is an inherited verb, from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}
